title: Your seeking is from Him
hookLine: the fact that you seek Him is already His gift
tomorrow: a door opens and you feel underqualified. walk in?

cards: A playlist that knows your mood before you do. An ad for the shoes you mentioned once, out loud, near your phone. Some days it feels like every want you have was planted by something.
Ibn Ata'illah, long before any feed, asked the same question about the best want of all: the wish to come close to God. Who put the wanting in you in the first place? You, or Him?
Inside Islam there are two honest ways to lean, and today both get to speak.

teach.b: The first voice leans on effort. The Qur'an says that those who strive for God's sake, He will guide to His paths.

teach.h: A HAND'S SPAN, AN ARM'S LENGTH.
teach.b: Al-Bukhari keeps a hadith qudsi, God's words told by the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him: whoever comes near to Me by a hand's span, I come near by an arm's length; whoever comes walking, I come running.
The person moves first, and God answers bigger. Its best point: it keeps you responsible. Nobody wakes up for fajr on your behalf.
The second voice leans on gift.

teach.h: TWO: THE SEEKING IS HIS GIFT.
teach.b: Ibn Ata'illah, paraphrased: the fact that you're seeking Him is already His gift to you. You wouldn't want Him unless He had put the wanting there. This side has its own verse: you will not will, unless God wills.
Its best point: it guards against pride. Your prayer streak isn't a trophy, because even the first step was handed to you. Notice that neither voice tells you to do less.
The effort voice doesn't say grace is unreal, and Ibn Ata'illah never says skip the alarm.

Plenty of room, then, to hold both at once: strive with everything, and thank Him for the striving. The real difference is what comes first in the heart when you notice you want to pray. One voice says, I showed up.
The other says, I was invited.

how: In Muslim teaching, striving in worship goes together with thanking God for the ability to strive; saying alhamdulillah after a prayer treats the prayer itself as a gift.

games.q: what does “your seeking is from him” mean?
o: you must earn God before you may seek Him
the wish to find God is itself God's gift
seeking God means leaving ordinary life

games.q: who says what — tap the pairs.
p: strive, and thank Him for it

s: if seeking God is His gift, your effort doesn't matter
neither voice says do less. Ibn Ata'illah never says skip the alarm.
a hadith qudsi says: come walking, and God comes running
kept by al-Bukhari: a hand's span answered with an arm's length.
Ibn Ata'illah says the wish to seek God is already His gift
you wouldn't want Him unless He had put the wanting there.

games.q: you lean toward the effort side. a friend says, 'it's all gift; my effort is nothing.' state her side at its best.
o: it keeps her from treating her prayer like a trophy to show off.
it means she can skip prayer until she feels the gift arrive.
it proves effort is pointless, so nobody needs to try at all.
games.why: the gift voice guards against pride: even the first step was handed to you. it never excuses skipping the steps.

practice: On your fingers, count three moments when you wanted something good: to be kinder, to pray, to forgive someone, to start over. It doesn't matter whether you followed through.
For each one, give a quiet thank you, to God if you pray, or simply to the wanting itself for showing up.

wordCard.voice: Your seeking is from Him: Ibn Ata'illah's reminder that the wish to come close is already a gift, not a trophy.

orig.note: Arabic: seeking, searching; the seeking Ibn Ata'illah calls His gift.

carryVoice: For the alarm tomorrow morning: the wanting is His gift, and so is the alarm you set for it. Five sayings down.

sources.ref: Ibn Ata'illah al-Iskandari, al-Hikam (the aphorism that your seeking Him is from Him)
Qur'an 29:69 (those who strive for Us, We will guide in Our ways)
Sahih al-Bukhari 7405 (hadith qudsi: a hand's span, an arm's length; walking, running)
Qur'an 76:30 (you will not will unless God wills)
